issues.description: The solution repository does not provide the expected concrete classes Seal, Pig, and Goat described in the problem statement and shown in the UML. Instead, it supplies classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (with matching behavior), while the files Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java in the solution are empty. This mismatch between expected class names (Seal, Pig, Goat) and the solution's concrete class names (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat) will confuse students about which classes to implement and may break automated tests or example code that reference Seal/Pig/Goat.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide concrete classes with the expected names (Seal, Pig, Goat) in the solution repository that implement the specified interfaces and constructors, or rename the example usages and the problem statement to consistently use SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat. Concretely: either (a) add Seal, Pig, Goat classes with the same implementations as SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat, or (b) update the problem/template to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat everywhere so class names are consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (and expect implementations with those exact names), but the solution repository implements these as SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (while Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java in the solution are empty). This mismatch forces students to map the conceptual entity names in the exercise (Seal/Pig/Goat) to different concrete class names (SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat) in the solution, creating unnecessary cognitive overhead and breaking direct requirement-to-implementation mapping.
issues.suggestedFix: Align class names across artifacts: rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat in the solution to Seal, Pig, and Goat respectively (including constructors and usages), or provide concrete Seal/Pig/Goat classes that extend the corresponding Space* classes. Ensure the class names match those used in the problem statement and template so students can directly map requirements to implementations.
